key_insight: Temporal synchronization between video and music can be achieved by matching when and how much change occurs (temporal structure) rather than matching semantic content; this lets you transfer timing patterns across modalities without paired data.
problem_solved: Generates music that is tightly time-aligned with video events despite the lack of fine-grained temporal control in existing text-to-music models and without requiring paired video–music datasets.
method: Extract modality-agnostic temporal-change signals from video (e.g., event onset/rate, motion envelopes) as a timing scaffold.
Learn a cross-modal mapping that transfers this temporal scaffold to musical dynamics and rhythm in a zero-pair setting (no paired video–music training required).
Condition a music generator on the transferred temporal structure so the produced audio aligns in time with video events (matching when/how much change, not semantic content).
impact: Provides a practical way to produce time-locked soundtracks for video editing, games, and media production without expensive paired datasets, giving ML practitioners fine-grained temporal control over generative music.
